text:
maria: Trying to onboard a customer to Dedicated + VPC and hitting cert verify errors when using the Python SDK behind their HTTP proxy :facepalm:
kevin: Can you paste the minimal repro and the exact error?
maria: Sure — code is tiny:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(base_url='https://private.redwood.internal', api_key='sk-xxxx', proxy='http://proxy.corp:3128', ca_cert='/etc/certs/corp-root.pem')
resp = client.generate('hello')
```
And the error: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain`
ak: do you mean you passed ca_cert to the client ctor? I don't see that param in our typed AsyncClient/Client signatures — might be a typing mismatch.
maria: I passed ca_cert because that's what our sample app suggested, but the SDK ignores it and uses requests/aiohttp defaults.
aj: Quick workaround: set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/certs/corp-root.pem for sync or for aiohttp create an SSLContext and pass to the connector. Not great for DX though.
kevin: Thanks. Can you try export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE first to confirm it's the ca chain?
maria: Confirmed — with REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE set it works. So two issues: 1) sample app/docs recommended `ca_cert` param which doesn't actually wire into the transport; 2) typing for AsyncClient doesn't include an explicit param to accept ca path or ssl context so users are guessing.
sam_dev: I ran into this too. The typed Client signature is strict: base_url, api_key, timeout, proxy etc but nothing for `ca_bundle` or `ssl_context`. AsyncClient uses aiohttp.ClientSession under the hood but we didn't expose connector/ssl args.
kevin: This explains a support ticket where a customer couldn't set custom CA for their VPC host. We should: (A) fix the sample app/docs to show env var workaround and aiohttp example, (B) expose a `ca_bundle` and `ssl_context` param on both Client and AsyncClient, (C) add typing for those params and docstrings.
maria: Also noticed retry behavior — when the proxy returns 407 Proxy Auth Required the SDK retries without proxy-auth headers and fails silently (user saw timeouts). That should be surfaced.
aj: Yep, need better proxy auth handling and clearer error messages. Could add an early validation when base_url is private + proxy set to warn if ca_bundle is missing.
infra-bot: deploy: sample-apps/docs updated on staging (build 2026-03-18T09:12Z)
kevin: Action items: I'll open an umbrella issue and link two PRs: one to tweak docs/sample app, one to add `ca_bundle`/`ssl_context` to constructors and update types. Assigning to @sam_dev for the async typing patch, @maria for doc changes.
sam_dev: I'll start a PR for async client — plan: add Optional[str] ca_bundle and Optional[Any] ssl_context to signature, pass through to aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ssl_context) and set verify=ca_bundle for sync requests adapter. Will add tests that simulate self-signed cert with local openssl.
maria: I'll update the sample app and onboarding checklist to include: export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, how to build ssl.SSLContext for aiohttp, and a note about proxy auth.
kevin: Can we also add a small FAQ snippet in onboarding: "Dedicated base_url often needs custom CA in corp networks — here's how"?
maria: Yes, will add.
aj: Minor note: update the python SDK changelog and add a quick mention to the console onboarding UI so SREs know to include proxy instructions for customers.
kevin: I'll create the umbrella issue now and tag both PRs — will include reproduction snippet and the REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE confirmation.
maria: Thanks all — saving this thread for the onboarding doc update checklist.
kevin: Thanks — marking as tracked. :thumbsup:
